name: Blanched Almond
lede: Blanched Almond is a pale, warm cream, one of the named colors of the web.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Blanched Almond comes from the X11 and CSS color list, where it is among the pale yellows [1]. The library also finds a Ridgway match, in the 1912 standard on plate XXX, and an ISCC-NBS match in block 89, under the name Ivory Yellow [1]. The name itself, a peeled almond, has no recorded history in the books we hold.

Its closest neighbors are Papaya Whip, a near duplicate at 1.8, and [[bisque]] [1]. Next to [[ecru]] it is a little lighter and yellower, at a distance of 4.6 [1]. Compare it with [[cornsilk]] and [[linen]] among the pale creams [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Blanched Almond appears in 1.74% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, as photographed [2]. It is more common than 74% of the named colors and peaks in the 1900s, at 1.8 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 54% of cases [2]. John Singer Sargent is its most devoted painter here, with 14 of 287 works [2].
